text:
Marathon Petroleum stock dropped 5.65% today, capping a sharp six-day decline from $414.65 to $373.25. The timing aligns directly with escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran has attacked U.S. military installations in Kuwait and struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, while a third U.S. carrier entered the Gulf. These events typically create immediate uncertainty for refiners, even though oil prices have held relatively stable at $89.53 per barrel domestically. The market appears to be pricing in disruption risk to global energy flows through a critical chokepoint.

Refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), and U.S. oil inventories are substantial, which normally supports refiner margins. However, the geopolitical shock may be overriding the technical backdrop—investors seem worried about the broader consequences of sustained regional conflict on crude supply reliability and demand rather than focusing on current inventory levels.
